artifacts.summary: Empirically confirms hypothesis (a) STRUCTURAL via the incident's own subagent transcript: the task-lock/session-registry heartbeat calls in general-implementation-agent.md Stage 4D were never emitted (0/8 phase transitions), not emitted-and-failed; surveys all listed call sites and records placement decisions for the pid-liveness, fingerprint, and events.jsonl cross-session findings.

memory_candidates.content: When an agent-contract markdown file's documented bash snippet is suspected of not executing, check for a Claude Code subagent transcript at ~/.claude/projects/<escaped-cwd>/<session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<name>-<hash>.jsonl before reasoning from source alone -- it records every actual tool_use the agent issued (with args and tool_result/is_error), turning 'did this fire' from an inference into a direct grep/json-parse. Located via `grep -rl '<session-id-fragment>' ~` or `find ~ -iname '*<fragment>*'`.

This agent system's markdown agent/skill files mix two placeholder conventions inconsistently: `$var` shell-variable form (meant to be substituted into an actually-executing bash command) versus `{token}` brace form (meant to be substituted textually into a downstream prompt/template string, e.g. a --session argument passed to another subagent's prompt). When auditing whether a documented bash snippet is reliable, check which convention it uses -- brace-form snippets passed directly to bash are a stronger signal of unreliability (an unsubstituted literal placeholder reliably breaks numeric-arg parsing, e.g. `printf "%03d" "{x}"` exits 1) even before checking whether the snippet fires at all.
